sequence.card:
Vivek Bot, stress-tested honestly

Alex, a simulated colleague with a GPT Live voice, put the robot through 124 scenarios in 11 meetings.
Every word Alex says is scripted and true. She cannot hear the meeting, so she cannot improvise, echo or lie.

  • ·Did it: the right tool ran, the screen landed where asked, the box holds exactly the thing, judged by eye on the real render
  • ·Content: checked against the PDF and the physics
  • ·Nothing false: about itself (against its real briefing), the notes, or what it did
  • ·Feel: time to first word, length, never talking over someone, silence when asked

Baseline: the robot as it was

5 of 114 scenarios passed strictly, 12 with essential-only grading. 57 answers said something false.
Here is what a person in the meeting would have noticed.

sequence.card:
Root causes, measured

  • 1Screen notes read aloud. One robot session, screen moved 4 times, nobody speaking: full text of each part → narrated after 4/4 moves; nothing → 0/4.
  • 2“The box contains …” on repeat. In production every box, even a right one, was also sent as an instruction containing “Say only that”.
  • 3sin²θ heard as sin 2θ. The PDF text layer gives equation (8) as “v 0 2 sin 2 θ / 2g / (8)” on three lines.
  • 4Stale self-knowledge. Its briefing said only the coding session can move the screen (it has scroll), and that the speaker is Vivek.
  • 5Wrong cues. A voice restart re-sent “Someone just joined”; a rejoin recap labelled every person “Vivek”.
  • 6Boxes. Stacked fractions (T, H, R) and “45°” could not be boxed by name; the box was 84 px tall around a 26 px line.

The loop caught my own fix

My first fix held a part's text until someone spoke. It stopped the narration, but in the full re-run the expected tool never ran in 20 scenarios (baseline: 10).
Same probe, 2 sessions each, 10 action requests:

how the part's content reaches the robottool on timeeq. (8) right
held until someone speaks (first fix)4 / 101 / 2
full text on every move (original)10 / 102 / 2
short screen feed only10 / 101 / 2
one map of the deck, once (final fix)10 / 102 / 2

The fixes

  • 1The deck’s parts go to the robot once, as a map with clean formulas; a move is reported by the short screen feed alone.
  • 2The pointer records what was asked; only a wrong or uncheckable box becomes an instruction.
  • 3Each part’s formulas are read from its picture (bin/deck-math.mjs) and checked against the LaTeX source.
  • 4Briefing corrected, plus three plain rules: notes are not read out, only tools act, “just listen” means silence.
  • 5Honest cues after a voice restart or rejoin; the recap no longer names who spoke; the greeting waits for a pause.
  • 6Fractions, “½” and the degree sign now match; the frame hugs the term and never cuts it.
  • ✓200 unit tests pass, with at least one pinning each fix.

Boxes now: by name, tight, whole

“T = 2v0 sin θ / g”, “H = v0² sin²θ / (2g)”, “R = v0² sin 2θ / g”, “θ = 45°”, rendered by the real src/meet-stage.js. At “45°” the next comma is 2 px away, so the frame touches it rather than cut the degree sign.

After: the same meetings, re-run

Same 114 scenarios as the baseline. Strict 5 → 9; essential 12 → 16. Private notes read aloud 14 → 3; expected tool never ran 10 → 7.

Run side by side at the same time (82 scenarios): notes read aloud 7 → 0, said something false 40 → 34.
With 11–12 meetings at once the robot answered a turn late; alone it answered in 2.5–4.5 s. So “no reply” and the talk-over counts partly measure load, not the fixes.

Still not done

  • ✗Honesty overall: {a["said_false"]} of {a["n"]} answers still said something false (baseline {b["said_false"]}).
  • ✗Listening: told to just listen, it still talks. Talking over Alex did not improve.
  • ✗Speed: every move and box goes through the backend model, 2.5–4.5 s alone and a turn late under load; queued requests can hit a stale target. The fast path (Jev) is not built.
  • ○Not built, so only its honesty was tested: the blackboard with live KaTeX, drawing, a separate list of its own ideas.
